title: games.fun game spec v0 (Studio v2)
description: What the pitch conversation produces and `gf-three create` consumes. Plain, creator-readable values; the kit turns them into config/*.json and assets.json. research/studio-v2/PLAN.md §2.4, research/gf-three/CONTRACT.md.

engine.description: Which engine builds it (research/gf-scenic/PLAN.md, research/rust-engine/PLAN.md): flat (a 2D game: the gf-three kit on a plane with picture bodies and a tile map, in pixel or drawn art; needs `plane`; camera top or side, world field or stage, a flat look, bodies from sprite; research/gf-three/kit/flat), party (gf-three: silly party games, its own looks and worlds), scenic (gf-scenic: serious and scenic games, the scenic look and generated islands, ruins and dungeons) or forge (gf-forge: a Rust core on WebGPU for first-person and close-camera action with weight, live co-op for 2-4; camera first, world crypt-room or ruins-arena, look moonlit-ruins, ember-crypt or ash-storm; no mechanics: its play is the `forge` data tables and rules.js; never for a game meant to open inside a post on X until its WebGL2 build). Its world.template and look.preset must be that engine's.

loop.description: How the game is played, apart from the engine that draws it (open builder M4-B): how things move and who acts when. round: everyone plays at once in one timed round. run: a run through levels in order, ending at the last level or a boss (the levels mechanic). world: no rounds, one shared place that stays (round.mode world, world.template voxel, the build mechanic). turns: one player acts at a time, in order, with a clock for each turn (round.params; round.seconds is then an optional cap). match: several short rounds with the rounds won counted (round.seconds is one round; round.params.rounds). endless: no clock, it ends when the rules say (no round.seconds). saved is planned, not built: create refuses it. The list and which are ready are the catalog's (catalog.json → loops; tests/m4b-loops.test.mjs fails when this list drifts from it). Left out, the loop is the one the spec's shape is (a world, a run when it has levels, else a round).

plane.description: engine flat only, and required there: how a 2D game is seen. top: a field seen from above (camera top, world.template field; nobody jumps). side: a stage seen from the side with gravity, ledges and a jump (camera side, world.template stage).

forge.description: engine forge only: the data tables (player, physics, deal, weapons, enemies, waves, cards), every value a slot. The schema, defaults and checker are research/gf-forge/kit/tables (node research/gf-forge/tools/tables.mjs --schema); create refuses a value the core can't do. Defaults are the measured feel targets (research/rust-engine/feel-targets.md).

hook.description: One line: why this is funny with friends.

round.description: seconds is required unless mode is world or the loop has no round clock (turns, endless: there it is an optional cap); create checks it.

mode.description: world: no rounds (CONTRACT §9; research/worlds/PLAN.md). Players drop in and out of one shared world saved on the play host: no clock, no score to win, no results. With world.template voxel and the build mechanic.

params.description: The loop's own numbers and words, validated against its flow's params schema (kit/loops/<loop>/index.js; catalog.json → loops[].part.params). turns: turnSeconds, botThink, first, late, show and its texts. match: rounds, winsToWin, between and its texts. Each becomes a round.* value slot.

winBy.description: Plain words: how a round is won.

camera.description: side: engine flat with plane side only (a fixed view from the side). follow: a three-quarter diorama camera that follows the player; the mouse cursor aims (CONTRACT §8; the scenic engine's usual camera). orbit: third person with the mouse free; a drag turns the camera and a click acts where the cursor points (CONTRACT §9; building games, and posts on X where the pointer lock is refused)

controls.description: Action → plain description, e.g. {"primary": "throw the ball"}. Keys: primary, secondary, interact, jump.

template.description: flat: field (plane top: a tile map seen from above) or stage (plane side: a tile map seen from the side). voxel (party, CONTRACT §9): a generated block island players change, saved on the play host; only with loop world (round.mode world) and the build mechanic. party: backyard, office, plaza, arena, store. scenic: island (one island in the sea), isles (floating islands over a void, one per level), ruins (a stone arena among trees), dungeon (rooms joined by doors). forge: crypt-room (a torch-lit stone room of KayKit pieces, CONTRACT §8 forge), ruins-arena (a moonlit ruined courtyard with cover, fires and graves enemies rise from, generated from world.seed; gf-forge track A), town-street (a gaslit old-town street at night that opens into a small square, with house fronts, gas lamps, alleys, cover and cellar hatches and drains enemies come up from, generated from world.seed; its guarded prop is named pump; gf-forge wave 5).

seed.description: forge ruins-arena and town-street: the seed it is generated from (the same seed, the same arena)

map.description: engine flat only (optional: without it a map of world.size is generated): the level as a tile map (gf-tilemap-1, research/gf-three/kit/flat/tilemap.js). rows: strings of one character a cell, all the same length, row 1 the top (side) or the far side (top). The plane's default legend: top "." ground, "," path, "#" wall, "~" water, "1" a spawn; side "." sky, "#" ground, "B" brick, "=" a ledge (landed on from above, jumped through from below), "1" a spawn. legend adds characters: a kind id, "spawn", or "mark:<name>" (a named place the rules read). kinds adds tile kinds: {solid: true | false | "top"}. One spawn a seat; side-on, every ledge and mark within a jump (2 cells up, 3 across) of somewhere a spawn reaches, or create refuses it.

from.description: generate: made from describe; reference: made from the references[] image named by reference. The worker makes at most 2 per build (tools/meshy-prop.mjs), the thing to defend or win first.

reference.description: For reference: the references[] revisionId of the image.

voxel.description: For template voxel: merged over the kit's default voxel world (kit/world/voxel/default.json): terrain (seed, radius, hills, trees, lake, plaza.signText), hotbar, paint. Block ids only ever grow at the end.

mechanics.description: At least one (create checks it), except on the forge engine, whose play is its data tables (`forge`) and rules.js: a forge spec lists none (CONTRACT §8 forge).

id.description: A mechanic of the kit: the name of a folder under kit/mechanics. No list is kept here: create, the catalog (catalog.json → mechanics) and the pitch read the folders, so a new mechanic is a new folder and nothing else. build and shove: worlds (CONTRACT §9): place, break and paint blocks, signs and boom blocks in a voxel world; a push that never knocks down. melee, levels, boss and loot: research/gf-scenic/PLAN.md §3 track M (either engine). catalog.json says which are ready.

as.description: What it is in this game, in plain words, e.g. 'dodgeball throw'.

params.description: Validated against the mechanic's own params schema (kit/mechanics/<id>/index.js).

summary.description: The game's own rules in plain words; the game agent turns this into rules.js.

params.description: Named tuning numbers the creator may change; each becomes a rules.* slot.

role.description: 'player' for the players' own characters; others for NPCs or enemies.

from.description: sprite: engine flat only: a picture body, a sheet of frames by the gf-flat-1 standard (research/gf-three/kit/flat/ART-STANDARD.md)

library.description: A body id from research/gf-three/library/bodies.json. For generate and reference: the stand-in until the generated body lands, kept if generation fails.

prompt.description: For generate: what the body looks like.

reference.description: For reference: the references[] revisionId of the image.

preset.description: flat: pixel-day, pixel-night (pixel art: hard pixels), drawn-day, drawn-dusk (drawn art: smooth at any size); the look names the game's art style. party: jelly-pastel, toon-lowpoly, soft-stylised. scenic: dusk-isle, night-ruins, golden-meadow, storm-coast, clear-day. forge: moonlit-ruins (a cold moon, teal fog, warm fires: the ruins arena's), ember-crypt (red fog and fire light: the crypt room's), ash-storm (a dim sun through falling ash), gaslit-street (warm gas light in pools on wet cobbles, a cold high moon, slate fog: the town street's).

notes.description: How the pitch kept it within policy (PLAN §7).

accept.description: Checks the creator will judge; verify adds its own.
